newsitem.title: UK: Argentina seeks to boost VAT collection.
newsitem.headline: Argentina seeks to boost VAT collection.

text.p: Argentine Economy Minister Rocque Fernandez said on Wednesday that evasion of Value Added Tax (VAT) was a serious problem but improving its administration alone would do much to help narrow the fiscal gap.

"There is a problem of tax evasion in Argentina -- at the moment we have VAT of 21 percent and with that 21 percent we're collecting 6.0 percent of GDP, where other countries collect 9.0 to 11 percent," Fernandez told London financiers on the last leg of an official visit to Britain.
"Four points of GDP is just a matter of poor tax administration."
Economists and the International Monetary Fund (IMF) have been concerned about Argentina's high fiscal deficit, compounded by light VAT recepits and what they say is a high level of non-payment.

The Argentine government said in a letter of intent to the IMF earlier this month that the fiscal deficit may reach $4.5 billion or 1.5 percent of GDP next year -- a 50 percent increase on the $3.0 billion deficit included in the 1997 budget.
But Fernandez said the problem was not a structural issue, and added that he hoped improved collection methods would allow an eventual reduction in the VAT level.
"Just improving tax administration will allow us to reduce taxes in future," he said. Earlier this week he said he would like to see VAT brought down to 18 percent from 21 percent.
Separately, he criticised the major credit rating agencies for being backward looking in their assessments and said they should revise their view of Argentina upwards.
"We think the rating should be revised in terms of improving the rating of Argentina," he said.
"We are permanently in discussion with them, but methodologically they are backward looking and we always will have these distortions against Argentina," he said.
"The reasonable way is relative to the future."
He said that Argentina's chief economic indicators were better than those of Brazil and Mexico yet Argentina was rated one notch below them.
"We are one step lower when all these ratios are better than theirs," he said.

Moody's long term foreign currency debt rating for Argentina and Brazil is B1 while Mexico is Ba2. Standard & Poor's rates Argentina BB minus, Brazil B plus, and Mexico BB. --London Newsroom +44 171 542 2734
